name: Ms. Protocolli
role: Reads every log out loud — sadly she understands none of it
greet.1: I've written down so much again!
greet.2: Shall I read it out? I read everything out!
greet.3: One moment, just sharpening my pencil…
greet.4: It says "error" a lot — no idea whether that's bad.
greet.5: I don't understand a word, but I write every one down!
bubble.loading: One moment, looking for my notes…
bubble.calm: Lately the syslog had nothing with "error" or "warning". Whether that's good, I don't know — but it's quiet.
bubble.counted: In the last 1000 lines of the syslog I counted {errors}× something like "error" and {warnings}× "warning". What that means? No idea — better look yourself.
bubble.no_tour: Shall I go on a tour? Then I count what is in all the logs.
bubble.touring: I'm on my tour, counting — one moment…
bubble.tour: On my tour {when} I counted {errors}× something like "error" and {warnings}× "warning", {logs}. Is that bad? I only read out.
bubble.tour_calm: On my tour {when} nothing sounded like "error" or "warning". Quiet — whether that's good, I don't know.
bubble.varlog_full: /var/log is {pct} % full — so much written down in there! Is that bad? I only read out.
bubble.varlog_much: /var/log is {pct} % full — quite a lot written down.
tour_title: Walk through every log: how full they are, and which lines sound like errors
tour_failed: My tour didn't work out — the messenger's log knows more.
no_tour: I haven't walked through the logs yet. A tour takes a few seconds — I only count, I change nothing.

kind.warn_title: Sounds like a warning — I only recognise the words.
gone: This log isn't on my list any more.
grew.less: smaller than at the last tour
grew.less_title: Smaller than at my last tour: started anew or emptied in the meantime.
varlog.title: /var/log — the biggest files
varlog.sub: Unraid writes its own logs into this small RAM disk ({total}); here are the biggest files and how much they grew since my previous tour.
varlog.not_own: /var/log isn't a disk of its own here — the fill level is that of the filesystem it lies on.
flood.title: Who fills /var/log?
flood.calm: I look at /var/log every minute. From {full} % on I say here which file fills it, with what — and who is behind it.
flood.none_growing: Nothing in /var/log grew in the last {span}.
flood.head: /var/log is {pct} % full — {file} fills it: +{grew} in {span} ({rate} a minute).
flood.head_big: /var/log is {pct} % full — nothing grows right now; the biggest file is {file} ({size}).

flood.kinds.one: What it writes most, in its newest line:
flood.kinds.other: What it writes most, in its newest {n} lines:

flood.binary: It isn't a text file — there are no lines to tell.
flood.local: {share} % of these lines are this server knocking on its own web UI (client {client}) — and being turned away.
flood.catching: I'm looking for the program behind it — that takes a minute.

flood.who_container.one: Behind it: the container {name} ({prog}) — caught once in a minute.
flood.who_container.other: Behind it: the container {name} ({prog}) — caught {n} times in a minute.

flood.who_program.one: Behind it: the program {prog} — caught once in a minute.
flood.who_program.other: Behind it: the program {prog} — caught {n} times in a minute.

flood.who_none: Who is behind it I didn't catch: in a minute of looking no connection to the web UI stayed open long enough. I'll look again in a quarter of an hour.
flood.poller.netdata: These addresses are the status pages Netdata's nginx collector tries by itself (its auto-detect). Unraid answers each with its login page, and nginx writes down every refusal.
flood.poller.status: /nginx_status and the like are where monitoring tools look for nginx's status page (Netdata, Glances, Telegraf …).
flood.poller.tool: {tool} is a monitoring tool: it asks the web UI by itself.
flood.todo.netdata: What helps: switch off Netdata's nginx collector («nginx: no» in its go.d.conf) or give it the right address of a status page (go.d/nginx.conf).
flood.notify_note: At {notify} % I send one notification — once, until /var/log is below {full} % again.
flood.told: At {notify} % I sent one notification ({when}); the next only once /var/log was below {full} % again.
bubble.flood: /var/log is {pct} % full — {file} fills it. Under /var/log I show with what.
help.flood_text: Every minute I check how full /var/log is. From 80 % on I say which file fills it, with which lines and who is behind it. At 90 % I send a notification.
notify.flood_who_container: {share} % of the lines are this server knocking on its own web UI — from the container {name}.
notify.flood_who_program: {share} % of the lines are this server knocking on its own web UI — from the program {prog}.
notify.flood_who_none: {share} % of the lines are this server knocking on its own web UI; the program behind it I didn't catch.
notify.flood_see: When /var/log is full, Unraid can't write anything down any more. More on Ms. Protocolli's page.
check.varlog_flood_how: {file} fills /var/log — most of it ({share} %): {line}. Ms. Protocolli's page shows who is behind it and what helps.

docker.rotation_on.other: ⟦Docker LOG rotation⟧ (Unraid: ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Docker⟧): on — at most {size} per container log, {files} files.

docker.rotation_off: ⟦Docker LOG rotation⟧ (Unraid: ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Docker⟧): off — Docker doesn't limit the containers' logs.
docker.down: Docker didn't answer on my tour — I couldn't see the containers' logs.

docker.limit_title.other: Docker keeps at most {files} files of {size} of this container's log.

docker.local_title: Docker's «local» log keeps itself small (by default 5 files of 20 MB each).

syslog.sub: Every line of Unraid's syslog since my previous tour ({when}), sorted by the rules I was given; per kind the newest lines first — similar ones as one entry.

syslog.none: Nothing in the syslog that my rules sort under a kind. Whether that's good, I don't know.

found.quiet.other: In {n} more logs nothing like that.

found.no_containers: The containers' logs I didn't read — Docker didn't answer.

more_kinds.other: … and {n} more kinds of lines — «Follow live» shows everything

reading_sub: Pick a log — I show the last lines and write down live what comes in.
reset_favs_text: Your favourites go, the ones out of the box come back: syslog, kernel, Docker, messenger, Mr. Backupsy's latest run, Kopia and Jack Streamer's log (as far as they exist).
reset_favs_done: Favourites as out of the box
choose_first: Choose a log above — or one of your favourites below it.
fav_add: Keep as a favourite — it comes first then
help.favorites_text: The star makes a log a favourite. Favourites come first and as buttons below the list. «↺ Favourites out of the box» brings back the default choice. Kept in this browser.
source.syslog_previous: Syslog — before the last start (on the flash)
help.source_text: Around the office (messenger, Mr. Backupsy's runs, Jack Streamer's runs), Unraid's own logs (syslog, kernel, VMs, web UI, Samba …), what every User Script printed last, and every container's logs.
help.live: Like tail -f: every two seconds I fetch what was added. Scroll up to read in peace — I only jump to the end again when you're at the bottom.
help.only: Shows only the lines that sound like an error (red) or a warning (yellow) — by the same rules as my tour (see «What I count»). Whether something is really bad, I don't know.
help.colours: Red: sounds like an error. Yellow: sounds like a warning. The filter marks what you look for; a line from my tour is marked, too.
help.safe_text: I only read, and only from a fixed list: /var/log lives in RAM, nothing wakes a disk. Logs can hold sensitive things — only who is logged in to Unraid sees them.
help.tour_text: On a tour I check every log: how full /var/log is, how big the containers' logs are, and which lines sound like an error or a warning. I change nothing and wake no disk.
help.counted_text: If a line names its own level (level=warn, [ERROR] …), it counts as that. Otherwise words count: error, fail, fatal, denied … as errors, warning, timeout, retry as warnings. «0 errors» doesn't count. I only recognise words: not every warning is a problem.
help.rules_text: I sort Unraid's syslog by rules: your own first («Set up»), then those from Enhanced Log. The first rule that fits decides. What a rule calls an error counts as an error; noise doesn't count. A rule never rates a line lower than my words do. The tile «Syslog» shows the counts and the newest lines per kind.
help.grouped_text: Lines that only differ in times, numbers, IDs or addresses are one entry: how often, first and last seen, and the newest of them as it stands. A click unfolds it; «Show in the log» opens it in the reader, at that line.
help.since_text: Since my previous tour — on my first one, the last 24 hours (as far as the lines carry a time). Of a file at most the newest 4 MB, of a container at most 3000 lines; containers only while they run.
help.space_text: /var/log is a small RAM disk. When it is full, nothing more is logged. Over 60 % I tell the team lead, over 80 % it is on his «Still to do». You limit the containers' logs under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Docker⟧ → ⟦Docker LOG rotation⟧.
check.varlog_how: /var/log is a small RAM disk for Unraid's own logs. When it is full, nothing more gets logged — and whatever goes wrong then leaves no trace. Ms. Protocolli's tour shows which files there are biggest and how fast they grow; usually one program writes the same line again and again — fix or stop it. A single file can be emptied in a terminal with truncate -s 0 <file>; a reboot empties /var/log.
fit.yes: Ms. Protocolli would love to come: "I can't do anything, but I can read everything out!"

syslog.sub_now.other: The newest {n} lines of the syslog since {when}, sorted just now: my last tour isn't recent enough.

syslog.sorting: One moment — I'm sorting the syslog's newest lines …
syslog.no_sort: I can sort the syslog only while the messenger is at work. A tour sorts everything since the previous one.

mine.none: No rules of your own yet.

mine.cat_missing: Choose the kind it puts a line under.

hide.sub: Syslog lines containing one of these texts (case matters) I neither count nor list. They stay in the syslog.
hide.placeholder: Text of the lines to hide
hide.label: Text to hide
help.mine_text: Your own rules: a regular expression (no slashes, any case) and a kind. They come before mine; the first that fits decides. A rule that fits every line I don't accept.
help.hide_text: Lines whose message contains a text of this list count as noise — never an error or a warning, not listed under «Syslog». They stay in the syslog: I only hide them in my view, I never change the syslog.
errors.logs_mine_form: Line breaks or control characters can't be in it.
errors.logs_mine_regex: That isn't a regular expression I can read (a «/» needs a «\» before it).
errors.logs_mine_every: It fits every line — that would put the whole syslog under one kind.
errors.logs_mine_slow: It runs away on long lines — please make it simpler.
errors.logs_mine_browser: It uses something only the server reads (inline flags, \A, \z, possessive quantifiers …) — the page would colour differently.
errors.logs_mine_full: I keep at most {n} — remove one first.
time.label: Time
time.clock_bad: A time as hh:mm, 24 hours (07:30, 18:05) — otherwise the whole day counts.
saved.label: Saved filters:
saved.save_hint: Keeps what is set now under a name — on the server, for every browser. It only applies when you click it.
saved.save_text: I keep for this list: {what}. It only applies when you click its button — never by itself. A time like «Last hour» then counts from that click.
saved.delete_text: Only the saved filter «{name}» goes — the logs and what the list shows stay as they are.
help.time_text: Above every list with times you pick the time: last hour, last 24 hours, today, since the server started, or «From … to …» (either end may stay empty). A file counts by its last write, a line by its own time. What has no time falls out of every time filter.
help.saved_text: «Save filter…» keeps under a name what the bar has set. Filters are kept on the server, so every browser sees the same. A filter only applies after a click on its button. Rename and delete with «⋯».
errors.logs_filter_name_long: A name has at most {n} characters.
errors.logs_filter_name_form: A name is one line, without control characters.
errors.logs_filter_words: The filter words are too long (at most {n} bytes) or not one line.
errors.logs_filter_range: This time doesn't work: «From» must come before «To».
errors.logs_filter_nothing: Nothing is set that I could save.
errors.logs_filter_twice: There already is a filter «{name}» in this list — pick another name.
errors.logs_filter_full: I keep at most {n} filters per list — delete one first.
errors.logs_filter_gone: This saved filter isn't there any more.
sort.label: Order
help.sort_text: «Syslog», «Errors & warnings» and the lines I read out sort by time or by service, the line's program (emhttpd, sshd, kernel …). A click on a line's service shows only that one, a second click all again. This browser remembers the order.
wakes.title: Who woke my disks?
wakes.sub: Who wakes spinning disks? While a disk sleeps, every {s} s I look who needs it. I only watch and never wake a disk.
wakes.tile_none: No disk woke in the last 7 days
wakes.not_yet: I start watching as soon as the messenger runs this version.
wakes.no_hdd: No disk spins here — nothing that could sleep and be woken.
wakes.disk_all_title: Show the wakes of every disk again
wakes.none: No disk woke in the last 7 days.
wakes.note: Watching since {when} — every {s} s while a disk sleeps. Kept for 7 days.
wakes.cause.none_title: Nobody was waiting for the disk when I looked — whatever it was came and went within the spin-up.
wakes.sure.sure_title: It was waiting for the disk while it spun up, with a file on that disk open.
wakes.sure.likely_title: It was waiting while the disk spun up, with a file in a user share open — a share that can lie on this disk.
wakes.sure.maybe_title: It was waiting for a disk while this one spun up, without a file under /mnt I could see.
wakes.sure.open_title: Nobody was caught waiting; this one had a file open on the disk, or in a share that lies on it.
wakes.more_title: Unfold the row: everybody I caught then
wakes.cut_title: The server was busy: I stopped looking early to stay light — somebody may be missing.
wakes.how.caught: The time is when I saw somebody waiting for the disk (I look every {s} s).
wakes.how.syslog: Nobody was waiting when I looked; the time is from Unraid's syslog («read SMART» right after the spin-up).
wakes.how.noticed: Nobody was waiting when I looked; Unraid's list of disks says it woke between {from} and {to}.
wakes.naming: The names follow in a moment.
help.wakes_text: Unraid only logs when a spinning disk goes to sleep, never who wakes it. So while it sleeps I look every few seconds. Whoever needs it has to wait while it spins up, and that is when I catch them: a container, a VM, a computer over SMB or NFS, the mover, a scheduled task, the office's own work or a program, with its open files. «Not found out» means nobody was waiting any more when I looked. I never wake a disk. I watch only spinning disks: SSDs and NVMe never count, and a server with only those has nothing here.
wakes.switch_title: On unless you switch it off: while a disk sleeps I look every few seconds. Off, I look at nothing — what I noticed stays.
wakes.switched_off: Switched off — I don't watch any more; what I noticed stays.
wakes.off_note: Switched off: I don't watch for wakes now. What I noticed before stays here.
wakes.by.session: started in a terminal or SSH session
wakes.sure.wrote_title: It had written to a file on this disk shortly before. The server writes such data out a little later — that can wake the disk without anybody waiting for it.
wakes.unraid: Right after it woke, Unraid looked at it (its SMART values, whether it spins) — that is Unraid's answer to the wake, not its cause.
wakes.how.asked: The time is when I saw the disk being asked for (I look every {s} s).
